title: VehicleGPT
description: VehicleGPT: an offline assistant design for a car's own signal data. A small model answers through verified tool calls; a 2-core CPU benchmark reached 82% accuracy at 1.74 s median.
lede: An offline assistant for a car's own logged signals. A small language model turns each question into one verified tool call on a read-only store, so the model never reads raw data.

blocks.text: Team entry to Tata Elxsi Teliport Season 4, Case 5. The proposal is an in-vehicle assistant that answers natural-language questions about the vehicle's own data, with no cloud connection.

Deterministic code ingests and stores the signals and detects events. A small language model, 2B parameters or fewer, only turns a question into one tool call, constrained to a flat JSON schema. Code checks the call against the signal catalogue, runs parameterised SQL, and checks that every number in the reply matches a query result.

blocks.caption: A CAN tap in listen-only mode and the VSS catalogue feed a read-only store. A small language model routes each question to one tool call, which is verified before it runs. The reply is written from the rows the call returns.

blocks.text: x86-64 CPU (AMD Ryzen AI 7 350), 2 cores, 2 threads, 2 GiB container memory, no swap. The hybrid pipeline is the rule router plus the model.

items: The CPU accuracy, latency and memory figures come from the first 50 questions, not all 200. Each configuration was run once, deterministically.
The data is synthetic. The CPU runs used an x86 proxy, not the ARM target board.
The rule router misroutes 4 of 50 questions, which caps tool choice at 92% for every model in the hybrid arm.
The in-car architecture (read-only tap, safety partition, privacy controls) is a design. The measured parts are the model routing and the tool calls.
